text: On one fixture, the app's list and `deep status --json` hold the same rows, IDs, words and order at one `log_pos`. A planted second order or a planted word fails, naming the row
`deep` prints the list and exits 0, and on a machine that isn't set up it runs setup first. A planted second count fails, naming it
With the hub stopped, `deep` prints the rows it can read from the database and says the hub isn't answering and since when, and no count reads 0
`deep inbox` prints each question before its handle, and `deep inbox answer <handle>` still works
An agent's `deep_status` holds no other session's asks. A planted row leak fails, naming the session
`992/agree` still holds, and every word comes from `states::TABLE`
Budgets, on the reference Mac in the local preflight, compared with the merge base: `deep` answers within 100 ms over the socket on 700 rows

An ask that defaults to No at 16:40 today reads "If you don't answer: No, at 16:40" in `deep inbox`, and its `--json` row holds `default` and `default_at`. A planted line with no default fails, naming the ask

With ten finished sessions of 30 calls each and two open asks, the last line of `deep status` is the count sentence and the output is under 40 lines. On the merge base it's over 200 lines and ends on a tool call
`deep inbox undo` says when the ask now defaults as a clock time in your time zone. On the merge base it prints a UTC timestamp and the test fails, naming the text
With open asks in three projects, each notification's title names its project. A planted title that holds a session ID fails, naming it
The fields the first criterion compares include unread. A planted `deep status` that disagrees with the app on unread fails, naming the row
